Fairlead 1.2.0 brings the mihomo-based tunnel stack to both platforms, clearer routing, and a round of UI and reliability work since 1.1.1.

## Both platforms

- Tunnel engine now uses mihomo (Clash Meta): TUN, DNS, WireGuard / AmneziaWG, and process rules in one place
- Clearer Direct / Through routing for IPs, domains, and apps
- Optional **Block browser QUIC** for tunnel traffic so browsers recover cleanly when rules change (Direct apps can still use QUIC)
- Smoother UI: pills, switches, notices, Amnezia badge
- Live rates and reachability while connected
- Language: Auto follows the system; English, Russian, German, Spanish, French, Portuguese, and Simplified Chinese
- Default tunnel: **None** stays off; Last active or a named tunnel is selected and connected on launch
- Helper-offline notice waits for startup instead of flashing immediately
- Notices slide in and out instead of jumping the layout
- Apps reconnect under new process rules without restarting the whole browser where the OS allows

## macOS

- Helper install / KeepAlive more reliable after login and updates
- Fixed a loop where a downloaded build kept asking for the administrator password even after the helper was already running
- Helper install strips quarantine from copied binaries so launchd can start them after a GitHub download
- Menu bar status and window behavior aligned with start hidden and default tunnel
- Route list uses icons instead of IP / Domain / App tags; clearer copy for domains and apps
- Auto language no longer sticks on the wrong locale after a previous preference

## Windows

- Native WinUI (C++/WinRT) app, aligned with the macOS layout and motion
- App list and filter UI fixes; smoother segment and switch animations
- Live metrics and localization brought in line with macOS
- When apps are added to the filter, their TCP sessions are reset so new rules apply without restarting the program
- Build and packaging fixes for the shipped `Fairlead.exe` + helper + engine layout
- Startup crash fix from the latest WinUI update
